sentences.text: A great teacher can change a student's life, but people disagree about what makes one great.
Some believe the most important qualities of a teacher are understanding and empathy, while others believe teachers should be rigorous and demanding.
I believe both qualities matter, and that the best teachers combine warmth with high expectations.
First, understanding and empathy are clearly vital qualities in a teacher.
Students learn best from someone who notices their struggles and believes in them.
For example, a patient teacher can give a frightened student the confidence to keep trying.
This shows that empathy can unlock learning that fear and pressure would only block.
A caring teacher also earns the trust that makes students willing to take risks.
Without warmth, even the most knowledgeable teacher may fail to reach her students.
To this extent, empathy is an essential teaching quality.
Second, however, being rigorous and demanding is just as important.
Students rarely reach their potential unless someone expects real effort from them.
Consider a demanding teacher who pushes her class to attempt work they thought was beyond them.
Such high expectations can draw out abilities students never knew they had.
A teacher who is only kind but never challenging may let students settle for too little.
Real respect for students includes believing they can meet a high standard.
Both qualities, then, are needed rather than only one.
In conclusion, empathy helps teachers reach and encourage their students.
But rigour matters too, since high expectations draw out a student's best.
The finest teachers combine genuine warmth with demanding standards, joining care and challenge together.
